title: Can PratiBimb's SHA-256 pin bind the exact ORT Web .wasm bytes to the bytes executed?

artifact_not_loaded.name: ort-wasm-simd-threaded.wasm
artifact_not_loaded.note: The NON-jsep artifact. ort.all.min.js does NOT load this one - measured. A different ORT bundle would load it, and would need its own pin.

ort.resolution_note: ort.all.min.js selects the JSEP build even for the 'wasm' execution provider. Measured, not assumed: the first run failed with "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: .../ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jsep.mjs". A different ORT bundle would load ort-wasm-simd-threaded.wasm and would need its own pin.

origins.collector: http://127.0.0.1:8910 (serves the artifact + tampered copy; in connect-src)
origins.foreign: http://127.0.0.1:8911 (serves the same artifact; NOT in connect-src)

packaging.why: The .wasm exists only on an arrival-logged origin. If ORT ever loads WebAssembly without our buffer it MUST fetch, and that fetch MUST appear in the arrival log. A packaged copy would make 'zero arrivals' ambiguous.

attribution: Our fetches carry x-pratibimb-probe; ORT's do not. An UNTAGGED artifact request is, by construction, ORT's.
isolation: ONE scenario per FRESH dedicated worker. ORT caches its WebAssembly module per JS realm; an earlier version of this harness ran all scenarios in one realm and produced a FALSE 'binding supported'.

machine_changes.REASON: The pinned runtime under test. Same version as W1-S03/S-04.
machine_changes.IMPACT: node_modules in this harness only; gitignored. Artifacts are 14-28 MB and are NEVER committed.

machine_changes.REASON: Regenerate the 174-byte W1-S03 model rather than invent a new one.

known_limitations: One machine, one OS. Chromium 151 + Firefox 155 on Windows.
Origins differ by PORT, not host. Cross-host/https untested (S-02a-2a-4a).
numThreads=1 throughout: deterministic, and avoids the worker-spawn fetch path. Multi-threaded ORT spawns workers that may fetch additional assets - NOT covered here.
The WebGPU execution provider was not exercised; only the 'wasm' EP. The jsep artifact is shared, but a WebGPU session may touch additional resources.
